content:
IncidentBot: :warning: canary-check:europe-west-1 FAILED — 5xx rate 12.3% over 5m (threshold 3%)

PagerDuty: :rotating_light: Pager triggered to @Maya R., @Sanjay P. (on-call) — incident key: pd_inc_1734020199

Maya R.: acked — jumping in. seeing the same in grafana: canary latency spikes ~200ms -> 1500ms and 5xx curve rising at 23:20 UTC.

Maya R.: quick triage: is this isolated to canary probes or visible from real traffic? @Lee (oncall) can you check prod top-level 5xx?

Lee (oncall): checking logs now. prod 5xx is flat at ~0.5% overall. looks isolated to synthetic canary runner in eu-west-1, but synthetic coverage hits model endpoints directly.

Cassidy: rolling up metrics link: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/6F3q9/canary-overview?orgId=1&from=now-30m

Maya R.: thanks. running curl to the canary endpoint from worker eu-west-1 to reproduce:

```
$ curl -v https://canary-eu-west-1.redwood-infra/probe/health
* Connected to canary-eu-west-1.redwood-infra (10.12.34.56) port 443 (#0)
> GET /probe/health HTTP/1.1
> Host: canary-eu-west-1.redwood-infra
> User-Agent: curl/7.79.1
> Accept: */*
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< content-type: application/json
< content-length: 128
{ "error": "upstream model-host connection refused" }
```

Maya R.: that 502 and "connection refused" suggests an upstream fleet or load-balancer routing issue rather than the probe runner itself. tagging infra. @InfraBot can you surface recent LB config changes?

InfraBot: no LB config changes in last 24h. Noted increased conn resets from host pool r-az3-euw-2 between 23:15-23:26 UTC. (logs id: infra-log-8912).

Sanjay P.: I'm taking lead. moving to mitigation steps: 1) pause canary alerts to stop pager noise 2) re-route canary traffic to fallback model-variant (v1.3 -> v1.2) 3) collect packet captures if needed 4) if insufficient, failover region.

Maya R.: executing step 1. Pausing alert rule canary-eu-west-1 for 30m to prevent repeated pages :white_check_mark: (alert-suppression id: sup-1734020205)

Lee (oncall): initiating reroute to v1.2 for canary runner. command: `./infra-tool routing set --service canary --region eu-west-1 --to-variant v1.2 --dry-run=false`

Cassidy: confirm: after reroute, canary results show 200 OK on the first two probes. still monitoring.

Maya R.: monitoring traces — initial reduction in 502s down to 1.1% in next 3m. looks like model-variant fallback mitigated errors.

Sanjay P.: good. action items: - keep canary paused until post-mortem - open ticket with model-hosting team to investigate why v1.3 host pool dropped connections - add alert suppression logic for transient LB resets - consider automated rollback on >5% 5xx within 10m. assigning tasks.

Maya R.: creating Jira: INF-4829 "canary eu-west-1 transient 502s due to model-host pool resets" and adding owners @InfraTeam, @ModelHosting. link: https://jira.redwood/browse/INF-4829

Cassidy: notifying customer-facing SREs in #support to pre-empt potential customer queries — no user-facing errors observed at this time.

Lee (oncall): handing off on-call to Sanjay (shift change). Sanjay, summary: canary-induced 5xx spike, paused alerts, rerouted canary traffic to v1.2, reduced 5xx to baseline. still collecting infra logs and retaining pcap for 1h.

Sanjay P.: thanks @Lee. I'll monitor for 60m then narrow suppression window. planning a coordinated post-mortem if model-hosting team confirms host pool instability.

IncidentBot: :white_check_mark: Incident resolved (canary stabilized) — automated page suppressed. incident closed at 23:40 UTC.

Maya R.: quick retrospection note: automated reroute + short alert suppression prevented customer noise. recommend adding an automatic short-circuit (15m) to reroute canaries to last-known-good variant on sustained 5xx. :bulb:

Sanjay P.: agreed. logging proposal to RFC tracker. thanks everyone for quick response :thumbsup:
